source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CloudHQ's LC8 in Ashburn publishes 756 MW of IT capacity, the largest disclosed power figure for any Virginia data center and about 29 percent of all published capacity in the state.

That share is as much about disclosure as about size. Virginia has 376 mapped facilities and only 29 publish a megawatt figure, so a single campus holding nearly a third of the disclosed total reflects how few operators say anything at all. The 756 MW is real, but it sits on top of a very small reporting base.

The density is the part that matters for AI. At 850,000 square feet of technical space, 756 MW works out to roughly 889 watts per square foot, well above a conventional enterprise data center and consistent with dense compute. Converting that to racks requires an assumption the operator does not publish: at 40 kW per rack it is about 18,900 racks, at 100 kW per rack about 7,560. Neither is CloudHQ's claim, and the accelerator count depends on chips per rack, which is also unpublished.

What the data does not cover is equally important. There are no certifications listed, so nothing here says what the campus is qualified to host. There is no announced expansion in the record. And 756 MW of published IT capacity is not 756 MW of delivered power: the grid connection behind it is the constraint that determines when, or whether, the capacity is usable.
